audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill/Skill/Skill/Jax/Skill/Jax/Jax while four of the whys[] beside them are written from Sett's side ('Sett still controls L2 short trades', 'Sett's L3 E-into-Q combo out-trades', 'Sett stays ahead L4-5', 'Sett's first-item Haymaker spike lets him re-enter').
audit.why: The mirror (jax__sett) settled the chart as Skill / Sett / Sett / Sett / Skill / Sett / Jax, and the packet chart agrees except at level 6, where the mirror and this page's own whys[4] both call it a genuine coin-flip.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 flipped to Sett in both layers as one atomic group with ratings moved to match (the mirror's 5/4/4/4/5/4/7 read from Jax's side inverts to 5/6/6/6/5/6/3 here). whys[0] and phases[0].why de-claimed so level 1 no longer reads as a Sett win on a Skill row.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said 'bait E' seven different ways without ever giving its cooldown, and named Jax's ultimate 'Grandmaster's Might' in the full layer and the level-6 spike.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s — long at rank 1 and still 9s maxed, which is what makes the bait-and-punish plan real. Leap Strike is 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s, Empower 7/6/5/4/3s, and the ultimate is Grandmaster-at-Arms per the kit file.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike's 17s at rank 1 and 9s at rank 5 keyed to the level-6 spike, first-item spike, mid and phases[5]; Leap Strike's 8s to the level 3-5 spike and phases[3]; the ultimate renamed Grandmaster-at-Arms.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated. Counter Strike dodges incoming ATTACKS — and Knuckle Down is an attack empowerment, so feeding it into an active Counter Strike throws away Sett's main damage. Haymaker is an ability, not an attack. The page instead said 'build armor' and 'don't W into his active E', which gets the priority backwards. Facebreaker is also called a stun with no mention of the opposite-sides condition.
audit.why: Riot's Jax E text: 'dodge all incoming attacks for a short duration and then quickly counterattack, stunning all surrounding enemies.' Riot's Sett Q text: 'Sett's next two attacks deal additional damage' — an attack empowerment. Riot's Sett W text is a cast, not an attack. Riot's Sett E text: 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.'
audit.corrected: Level-6 spike and mid now say hold Knuckle Down through the dodge window rather than spending punches into it, and cash Haymaker after the stun resolves; the opposite-sides condition written into phases[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Both applicable missing interactions were absent: Empower opens his combo with an auto-attack reset, and The Show Stopper is listed as shutting off Leap Strike and Empower.
audit.why: The reset means his wind-up is the tell, not the ability cast — that is what makes level 1 a coin-flip rather than a free Sett row. The Leap Strike denial is why R is held for his engage rather than spent on poke.
audit.corrected: Auto-reset tell written into phases[0].why. The R-denies-Leap-Strike claim I restated only as far as the kit supports — see notes; the mirror already published the stronger 'grounding' wording on Jax's page.

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Jax on every CS, but respect his opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Your double-punch passive out-hits him at 1, but Empower is a 7s auto reset — his wind-up is the cue to step back. Bank chips, don't coin-flip an all-in.

edits.before: Facebreaker is online — the E-stun into double punch + W is your full pattern. Run it the moment Jax burns Counter Strike.
edits.after: Facebreaker (16s) is online — it stuns only with a target each side, so pull him across your minions once Counter Strike is spent.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Jax has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier and Leap Strike (8s) is his only exit. Bait it into your minions, then punch in and cash W dead-centre.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Jax. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before he matches your item.
edits.after: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Jax. Force your trades while Counter Strike (9s at rank 5) is down, never into the dodge.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Counter Strike and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Sterak's keeps you alive, but Counter Strike (9s) dodges your punches and Grandmaster-at-Arms out-grinds your Grit. End it before his third item.

edits.before: Sett's L1 Q burst and E self-peel beat Jax before Empower stacks matter.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — you punch harder, but Empower (7s) answers each trade.

edits.before: With E Facebreaker plus Q Knuckle Down you win every short trade before Jax has enough Empower stacks to matter; his Q Leap Strike is his only gap-close, so bait it into minions and punish while it's down.
edits.after: With Facebreaker plus Knuckle Down you win the short trades before Empower ramps; Leap Strike (8s) is his only gap-close, so bait it into your minions and punish the window while it is down.

edits.before: Jax's R Grandmaster's Might turns even trades against him if he E Counter Strikes your all-in; hold your W Haymaker until his E stun window passes rather than eating the AoE stun, and it's a coinflip skill fight.
edits.after: Grandmaster-at-Arms turns an even trade against you the moment Counter Strike (17s at rank 1) eats your punches — it dodges attacks, so hold Knuckle Down through the dodge window and cash Haymaker once the stun lands.

edits.before: Your first-item spike on Haymaker true damage and grit lets you re-enter — pull Jax's E with a Q poke, then commit the real all-in once Counter Strike is on cooldown.
edits.after: Your first-item spike lets you re-enter — bait Counter Strike (9s at rank 5) with a single punch, then commit and cash Haymaker with Jax dead-centre, where the panel is true damage.

edits.before: You own levels 1-4: Q Knuckle Down plus E Facebreaker gives you burst and a self-peel before Jax's Empower ramps, and his only escape is Leap Strike — pull it and he's stuck taking your trade.
edits.after: Levels 2-5 are yours: Knuckle Down plus Facebreaker beat him before Empower ramps, and Leap Strike (8s) is his only escape — bait it out and he is stuck taking your trade.

edits.before: Level 6 is the swing point and it's genuinely a skill matchup: if you dodge his E stun window before dropping W Haymaker you win, but eat the AoE stun and his R sustained DPS flips it. Play around his Counter Strike cooldown, not raw stats.
edits.after: Level 6 is the swing point and genuinely a skill matchup: Counter Strike dodges attacks, so wait its window out instead of feeding punches into it, then cash Haymaker once the stun lands. Play his 17s cooldown, not raw stats.

edits.before: Once Jax has two-plus items his E dodges your Pit Grit autos and R lets him grind through your grit shield, so the matchup tilts to him — force a lead early and close before he online.
edits.after: Once Jax has two-plus items Counter Strike dodges your punches and Grandmaster-at-Arms grinds through your Grit shield, so the matchup tilts to him — force a lead early and close it out.

edits.before: Free stacks on Empowered Q into your face
edits.after: Free stacks with Empower autos in your face

notes: Fixed a broken sentence in the content layer: late ended '...close before he online.' Two naming problems: the full layer and spikes[1] called Jax's ultimate 'Grandmaster's Might' while the kit and packet both say Grandmaster-at-Arms (now corrected in the paths I touched, but the mirror notes the content layer also uses 'Grandmaster at Arms' unhyphenated in whys[4], whys[6] and elsewhere — one rename pass would settle it). The packet's suspectNames hit on 'Counter Strikes' was a false positive, but that sentence was rewritten for other reasons anyway. Two things I would not assert. First, the missing-interactions file says The Show Stopper 'shuts off' Leap Strike and Empower via a grounding flag that Riot's R description does not mention; the jax__sett mirror already published the grounding wording on its side, so the two pages are inconsistent in strength — someone should decide once whether Sett's R grounds, because three of my matchups this slice hit the same flag. Second, that Counter Strike dodges Knuckle Down's empowered punches follows directly from 'dodge all incoming attacks' plus 'Sett's next two attacks', but Riot never spells out the interaction; I rated it Medium and wrote it as attack-versus-ability rather than as a named mechanic.
